_note: The demo video, in order. kind 'scene' = a cartoon scene from tools/intro/story.html; kind 'app' = a recorded chapter from tools/record-demo.mjs (matched by title). Each item has the narration Brian reads over it (tools/narrate.py); the composer holds an item on screen until its line ends. The intro (tools/intro/intro.html) plays first with its own sound.

items.text: Vivian and Frank, from Australia, are planning a trip to Tanzania. Their friend Emma tells them about Noor's coffee farm, up in Materuni: no website, no phone line, no internet. You can only go by luck, she says.
But Emma left her feedback through WeKaribu. So Vivian opens it, and picks Visitor.

items.title: Find a place
items.text: She searches for Materuni. There is Noor's farm, with what twelve guests said about it, counts only, and the days Noor can take visitors next week. Noor published them a week ahead, from her own phone.

items.title: Book a visit
items.text: They pick Saturday, two guests, English, and mention Emma. WeKaribu remembers that Emma visited in September. The request goes to the tour company.
At Ondera Coffee Trails, Juma sees the request and confirms it. WeKaribu turns it into a plain text message.

items.title: Confirmed: an SMS for a basic phone
items.text: No app on Noor's side. Just an SMS, in Swahili, to a phone that costs twenty dollars.
Up on the mountain, Noor's phone beeps: two guests on Saturday, English speakers, with Juma. She knows who is coming, a week ahead, and which language to prepare.

items.title: Next week, on the helper’s phone
items.text: On the family's smartphone, next week shows the booking, and that the English pack is already there. Rare languages are downloaded only when a guest is coming, and deleted afterwards. Storage costs money.
Saturday. Vivian and Frank roast and grind coffee with Noor's family, and write in the paper guestbook. Other guests that week wrote in German, and one left a voice note in French.

items.title: Vivian writes on Noor’s phone
items.text: Noor can also hand over the phone. Vivian types in English, ticks that they would buy coffee beans, and agrees to be contacted.

items.title: A photo of the guestbook
items.text: The German page is photographed. A text reader on the phone reads it, and highlights the words it is unsure of.

items.title: A voice note
items.text: The French voice note is transcribed and translated on the phone, by Whisper. Nothing leaves the device.
On Sunday, Noor's daughter Amina comes home. In ten minutes, the whole week's feedback is in Swahili.

items.title: The week, in Swahili
items.text: The phone splits each comment into sentences, matches them to ten fixed topics, and reads the mood. The summary is built from sentences a person wrote; the AI only fills in counts. Sikiliza reads it aloud.

items.title: Check what the AI was unsure about
items.text: Every topic keeps the guests' own words. When the model is unsure, the sentence is marked Check, for a person. Unsure means ask a human, not guess.

items.title: A thank-you for Vivian
items.text: A thank-you note goes to Vivian, in English, human-written, because she agreed, and only when Noor taps send.

items.title: A report for the tour company
items.text: And a report with counts only, no names, no quotes, goes to the tour company if Noor agrees. That is how next season's tours get better.

items.title: Our take on localising AI
items.text: Our take on localising AI: keep the models language-agnostic through an English pivot, and keep every word a person reads human-written, in their language. A new host language is one translated file, not a new model. Chagga has no small model yet; the app says so instead of pretending.
WeKaribu: we welcome. Any host, any guest language, no account. Try it at wekaribu dot lovable dot app.
